 This Appeal Coming On For Admission This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 23.11.2013,
passed by the tribunal, in MVC No.153/2013, questioning the liability fixed on the insurance company.

2. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
3.
The factum of accident, death occurred due to accident are not disputed, except the insurance coverage.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10707 Reliance General Insurance vs Savita W/O Mallappa Agadi on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129294209/
2 4. The tribunal while awarding compensation has saddled liability on the appellant insurance company.
It is contended by the appellant that bus was not having valid and effective permit to ply on the road as there was no permit as on the date of accident.
Ex.R.8 is the letter issued by the RTO showing that permit to the bus was issued from 20.06.2013 to 19.06.2018 for a period of five years.
But the accident was caused on 04.02.2013.
Therefore there is no evidence on the part of either of the claimant or the owner that as on the date of accident bus was having permit to ply on the road.
Therefore it is proved that the bus was having permit to ply on the road w.e.f. 20.06.2013 but prior to this the accident was caused on 04.02.2013.
Therefore, it is amounting to plying the bus without permit.
Therefore respondent owner of the bus has operated the bus on the road without having permit is a fundamental breach of condition of policy.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the bus.

However even though as per sub-section (2) of section 149 of the M.V.Act, the insurance company is able to establish his defence but as per sub-section (1), (5) and (7) of section 149 of the M.V.Act,
and also as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of PAPPU AND OTHERS vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208;

entities.text: PAPPU AND OTHERS vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208

NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED vs. SWARAN SINGH AND OTHERS reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297; and also as per the Full Bench decision of this Court in the case of NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED vs. YELLAVVA AND ANOTHER reported in 2020 ACJ 2560,
the insurance company shall satisfy the claim at the first instance to the claimants and then recover it from the owner of the tractor.

Hence, the appeal is liable to be allowed in part.

6. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 23.11.2013, passed by the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Dharwad, sitting at Kalaghatagi, in MVC No.153/2013,
stands modified holding that the insurance company is exonerated from payment of compensation.
